body:
This a relatively simple fix for the scripted path in scene/main/window.cpp. We can add a check in Window::_update_viewport_for_hdr_output() and fire the warning (as written above). But it exposes another issue:

The Game View toolbar bypasses Window entirely. It calls DisplayServer::window_request_hdr_output() directly, so Window::set_hdr_output_requested() never runs.  A decision is needed whether this should be routed through Window or if it should be left as a separate path (and leave an inconsistency)

The spirit of `Window::set_hdr_output_requested(bool p_requested)` is to be a simple wrapper around `DisplayServer::window_request_hdr_output(const bool p_enable, DisplayServerEnums::WindowID p_window)` that is functionally identical.

So the fact that `_update_viewport_for_hdr_output()` can be skipped if you call this directly through the `DisplayServer` sounds like a bug.

...And indeed, from a quick test on my end, this does seem to be a bug: when I'm working with a project that has HDR 2D disabled, I get different behaviour when I enable "Request HDR Output" on the game view than if I enabled "Request HDR Output" through the project settings! This should not be the case and is a bug.

I'm not sure what the exact fix and cleanup should be, but this was a good find -- thanks hackenshaw! To fix the bug, the end result is that `Window::_update_viewport_for_hdr_output()` should always be called any time `DisplayServer::window_request_hdr_output(...` for that window is called. Additionally, I'm not entirely sure what the current purpose of the member variable `bool Window::hdr_output_requested` is... It seems that almost every time its used, it's updated from the display sever immediately before... But it's very possible I'm overlooking something and this member variable is needed for a very real reason that still exists.

It goes further: display_server.cpp:1563 binds `DisplayServer::window_request_hdr_output` to ClassDB, so any project can call `DisplayServer.window_request_hdr_output(true)` from GDScript and run into this issue!

My naive instinctive solution would be to prevent direct access to this method and make sure everything goes through `Window` where we can control it and stay true to the spirit of the wrapper. But that will break compatibility, so something more nuanced is needed.

As far as I can tell the member variable `bool Window::hdr_output_requested` is needed to hold the requested state *before* the OS window exists. Like in the inspector when you add a Window node. `Window::_make_window()` uses it to create the OS window.

> But that will break compatibility

I suspect the old behaviour may be better described as a "bug" from any practical perspective and therefore not a compatibility break... I believe it is simply a bug to get into a state where "request hdr output" is `true` on a Window and for that Window's main Viewport to not have HDR 2D behaviour. The reason this is a bug is because, in that state, the game will render a substantially different appearance depending on whether their operating system is running their screen in HDR mode or SDR mode -- And this is a bug in Godot to ever let this happen.

Does that make sense or is there something I'm missing that would better be described as a "compatibility break"? Or I am misunderstanding how things will play out in practice?

It makes sense, and I agree it's a bug. Should I just make a pull request with some attempt? Then we can go from there. 

My idea is:

- Fix `SceneDebugger::_msg_hdr_output_toggle_requested`  to route through `Window` instead of `DisplayServer`.
- Fix `Window::_make_window()` so that a newly created Window that becomes visible with `hdr_output_requested` already true and HDR 2D off gets the viewport forced on.
- Add the warning from the original description in `Window::_update_viewport_for_hdr_output()`
- Leave the binding alone (knowing that calling `DisplayServer.window_request_hdr_output(true)` from GDScript will remain an issue)

Hmm, you can go ahead and make the PR, of course, but I expect that it won't make sense to merge anything that doesn't also completely fix all discrepancies between `Window::set_hdr_output_requested(bool p_requested)` and `DisplayServer::window_request_hdr_output(const bool p_enable, DisplayServerEnums::WindowID p_window)`.
